findings.claim: An SSE stream that dies mid-turn (connection closed before response.completed/response.incomplete) is reported as SUCCESS with the truncated partial text as the final value — data loss presented as a good result.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by probe p2 (/tmp/oai_probe/probe.baml): mock_sse_serve sends one delta {"delta":"par"} then closes with no terminal event; ai.stream.from_spec(...).final() returns "par" with no error. Root cause: TurnDone is documented optional — stream.baml:48-51 "a stream that simply ends (SSE close) also completes the turn" and final_turn (stream.baml:214-238) defaults stop_reason to Complete. The openai decoder (openai/ns_internal/responses.baml:884-897) knows whether a terminal event arrived but has no hook to signal EOF-without-terminal; PLAN §6 defers streaming tool-call deltas only, not truncation detection. OpenAI's stream contract always ends a successful stream with response.completed/incomplete/failed (openai-openapi ResponseStreamEvent, openapi.yaml:59681-59740), so a close without one is definitively truncation for this provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Give TurnStream a per-provider 'requires terminal event' mode (or an on_eof callback in from_sse): the openai decoder sets a saw_terminal flag in OaStreamState, and EOF without it throws ai.errors.NetworkFailure (outcome unobserved). Stdlib change + one flag in the openai decoder.

findings.claim: _openai_prune_nulls runs over the WHOLE serialized request including user-supplied tool JSON schemas, silently deleting legitimate null-valued object members (e.g. "default": null, "const": null) from tools[].parameters — the wire schema is not the schema the user declared.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by probe p1: a raw_tool schema {"city":{"type":"string","default":null}} renders on the wire as "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}}} — the "default":null entry is gone. Prune is applied at responses.baml:615-618 over baml.json.to_json(request), which includes the open-ended parameters json inserted at :498. The prune's own comment (:200-204) says it exists only to drop the typed request classes' unset optionals; user JSON is collateral. sys_llm never altered user schemas (serde skip_serializing_if on its own fields only). Docs: FunctionTool.parameters is an arbitrary JSON schema map (openai-openapi openapi.yaml:68003-68010).
findings.suggested_fix: Prune only the typed layers: either serialize tools[].parameters (and any request_body content) AFTER pruning, or make _openai_prune_nulls stop recursing into the parameters subtree (e.g. prune the request with parameters temporarily replaced by placeholders, or add an exempt-keys parameter).

findings.claim: A streamed refusal (or max-tokens truncation) is invisible to the typed stream: the terminal stop_reason the openai decoder correctly computes is folded into TurnStream state but ai.stream.Stream.final()/next() never consult it, so a refusal-only stream returns an empty-string SUCCESS while the non-streaming path throws ai.errors.Refused.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by probe p10: mock SSE sends only response.completed whose message content is [{"type":"refusal","refusal":"I cannot help with that."}]; ai.stream.from_spec(...).final() returns "" (no error). The openai decoder does its half right — openai_parse sets StopReason.Refused (openai/ns_internal/responses.baml:703-706, 745-746) and emits it in TurnMeta (:886-895) — but from_spec's Stream pulls only text deltas (stream.baml:339-348) and final() SAP-parses accumulated text (:277-291) without checking TurnStream._stop_reason. Non-streaming Agent.run throws Refused on the same turn (ai/runner.baml:383-393). Also drops refusal deltas mid-stream (no response.refusal.delta arm), but the terminal-enforcement gap is the substantive defect. Not in PLAN §6 (which defers tool-call deltas only).
findings.suggested_fix: After the TurnStream reports Done, from_spec's _next_text (or Stream.final) should inspect turns' folded stop_reason and throw ai.errors.Refused / surface MaxTokens exactly like runner.baml does before SAP-parsing the final text.

findings.claim: A transient provider failure reported in-body — response.failed / error SSE event with code "server_error" (the docs' own canonical example) — is classified as ai.errors.InvalidRequest, which ai.Retry's default judgment never retries; the non-streaming 5xx path classifies the same condition as retryable NetworkFailure.
findings.evidence: _openai_error_failure (:645-661) maps only rate_limit/insufficient_quota → RateLimited and content_filter/moderation/refusal → Refused; everything else, including "server_error", falls to InvalidRequest (:653-660). default_retry_judgment returns false for InvalidRequest (ai/ns_clients/clients.baml:6-13). The docs' response.failed example is precisely {"code":"server_error","message":"The model failed to generate a response."} (openai-openapi openapi.yaml:57887-57900), a transient condition; the engine raised a retryable LLMErrorResponse for it (research §3). Asymmetry: an HTTP 500 goes through classify_http → NetworkFailure (probe p7 passed, "network:http 500"), but the same failure delivered as a 200/SSE body error becomes permanent. Existing test oai_stream_failed_event even pins the InvalidRequest classification.
findings.suggested_fix: In _openai_error_failure, map code "server_error" (and timeout-ish codes) to ai.errors.NetworkFailure so mid-stream/in-body transient failures stay retryable; update the oai_stream_failed_event expectation.

findings.claim: Per-message metadata (ai.PromptMessage.metadata, PLAN §5's accepted 'engine placement on content part' row and research G5) is completely dropped by the openai Responses client — sys_llm flattened @@meta onto the message and the engine merged it onto content parts; native sends nothing.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by probe p11: a prompt using ${baml.prompt.Role { name: "user", metadata: { "cache_hint": "yes" } }} yields meta_present_on_message=true on the rendered PromptMessage but on_wire=false in openai_render's body. grep shows zero references to `metadata` in openai/ns_internal/responses.baml or openai/responses.baml, while the anthropic client consumes the same field (anthropic/ns_internal/messages.baml:311 cache_control). PLAN §5 row 'Message metadata placement (openai): engine (content part)' is an accepted DECISION about placement, implying implementation; it is absent from PLAN §6 and from EXECUTION-STATUS's deferred-triage list (which defers only the role() helper's metadata *setter*, not client-side consumption).
findings.suggested_fix: In _openai_prompt_content, merge message.metadata keys onto each emitted content part (engine placement per PLAN §5), or record an explicit deferral in PLAN §6 if openai metadata is being dropped knowingly.

findings.claim: A function_call output item whose `arguments` string is not valid JSON escapes as a raw baml UnknownError(JsonParseError) instead of ai.errors.ParseFailed — provider-malformed output is not classified.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by probe p12: mock returns {"type":"function_call",...,"arguments":"not json"}; cl.invoke throws `UnknownError { data: JsonParseError ... }` (via invoke's catch_all + ai.errors.normalize passthrough of UnknownError), not ParseFailed. openai_parse calls baml.json.from_string<map<string, unknown>>(s) at :690 with no catch, unlike send_as's body decode which wraps in ParseFailed (ai/ns_wire/wire.baml:29-31).
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the arguments decode in catch_all → throw ai.errors.ParseFailed { provider: "openai", raw_output: s } (or fall back to an empty args map, matching lenient providers).

findings.claim: The streaming text dedup key ignores content_index: response.output_text.delta/done are keyed by item_id (or output_index) only, so for a message item with multiple text content parts, a done-only delivery of a second part is wrongly suppressed after any delta on the first part.
findings.evidence: _openai_event_key (:818-826) uses event.item_id/output_index; text_started.set/get at :852, :859-864 share one key per item. The API's ResponseTextDeltaEvent/ResponseTextDoneEvent both carry a required content_index distinguishing parts within one item (openai-openapi openapi.yaml:59770-59825, 59826-59881). Theoretical-only today (servers stream deltas for every part), no probe constructed; UNVERIFIED against live behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Key text_started by `${item_id}:${content_index}` (OaStreamEvent needs a content_index field).

findings.claim: Research matrix row G10 (finish_reason_allow_list / deny_list enforcement, sys_llm lib.rs:560-570) is neither implemented nor listed in PLAN §6 / EXECUTION-STATUS deferrals — the row is unaccounted for.
findings.evidence: ResponsesClient's option surface (responses.baml:17-54) has no finish-reason policy fields and openai_parse enforces none; PLAN §6's dropped-knowingly list names legacy /completions, client_response_type, o1 special-casing, IRSA/AssumeRole but not finish_reason lists. Likely an intentional drop (typed StopReason + Refused/MaxTokens handling supersedes it), but the audit trichotomy requires it be recorded somewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Add finish_reason allow/deny lists to the PLAN §6 dropped-knowingly list (or implement as a wrapper-client policy).

findings.claim: Stale doc comment: reasoning_effort is documented as "minimal" | "low" | "medium" | "high", but the current API accepts none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max.
findings.evidence: openai-openapi ReasoningEffort enum: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (openapi.yaml:56790-56800). Behavior is unaffected — the field is an unvalidated passthrough string — but the comment under-documents the accepted values (same for reasoning.mode/context, which are reachable only via request_body).
findings.suggested_fix: Update the comment (and optionally mention that other Reasoning subfields ride through request_body).
